title: Ten-year follow up of patients with first-episode schizophrenia spectrum disorder from an early intervention service: Predictors of clinical remission and functional recovery

Not the same sample as chang2016b, which is a later randomised trial of EASY 2-year completers.
notes: Employment is reported ONLY as mean months of full-time employment and mean months of unemployment over the initial 3 years (Tables 1-3, pp. 67-68), used as predictors of 10-year remission/recovery. Employment status WAS collected at the 10-year interview ('Demographic information including age, gender, education level, employment status were obtained', Methods 2.3, p. 66) but no employment count or rate is reported anywhere. No numerator and no denominator recoverable, so report_quantifiable = no and no outcome row is written. 'Months of unemployment including period of unemployment and rehabilitation' (table footnotes), so time in rehabilitation settings is counted as unemployment.

title: Ten-year employment patterns of patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum disorders: comparison of early intervention and standard care services
cohort_overlap_notes: COHORT CONFIRMED, and the report describes TWO separately recruited samples. The early intervention sample IS hk_easy_2001 (EASY, 1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002, schizophrenia-spectrum, 148 identified, 74.3% interviewed, N = 110), identical to chan2019 (which chan2020 cites as reference 22) and to the EIS group of chan2022. The standard care sample is a separately recruited historical control cohort (first presentation to standard care 1 July 2000 to 30 June 2001) and is recorded as hk_standard_care_2000 under D12.5 / codebook rule 11. extraction_reports carries only the index cohort; report_cohort_map.csv is authoritative and carries both.
notes: EMPLOYMENT IS THE STATED OUTCOME BUT NO COUNT IS RECOVERABLE. The 10-year employment history is expressed as months of employment per year, and the reported quantities are (a) hierarchical-cluster memberships (good employment cluster: early intervention 98/145 (67.6%), standard care 76/145 (52.4%)) and (b) mean total months of full-time employment in year 1. A trajectory-cluster membership is NOT a count of people employed at a timepoint and must not be read as one, so no employment prevalence row is written. CONSTRUCT, if a count is ever obtained: 'Patients who were in full-time or part-time competitive paid employment or full-time education (provided by a government-recognised educational institution) at any time during the assessment period were considered as employed for that period. ... Supported employment, volunteer work, working at a rehabilitation centre and part-time education were not included.' (Method, Ten-year employment history, p. 492). That is paid_or_education and explicitly EXCLUDES supported and sheltered paid work, so it could never serve as paid_any.

title: Longitudinal relapse pattern of patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and its predictors and outcomes: A 10-year follow-up study
cohort_overlap_notes: Re-analysis of the same 148 matched pairs as chan2020: the EIS group is hk_easy_2001 and the SCS group is hk_standard_care_2000, so two rows in report_cohort_map.csv. The analysed sample (n = 209) POOLS the two cohorts and is split by relapse timing, not by service, so it is not a whole-cohort analysis unit for either cohort. Table 1 confirms the composition: early intervention service 72 + 35 = 107, standard care service 81 + 21 = 102.
notes: Employment is reported ONLY as mean months of employment and mean months of unemployment over 10 years, by relapse group (Table 2, p. 4). No count of people employed at any timepoint. Cross-sectional 10-year outcomes are PANSS/SANS/CDS/SOFAS/RFS scores only; the RFS 'Work' subscale is a 1-7 functioning rating, not an employment count. No numerator or denominator recoverable, so report_quantifiable = no and no outcome row is written.

title: Three-year clinical and functional outcome comparison between first-episode mania with psychotic features and first-episode schizophrenia
cohort_overlap_notes: MANIFEST CORRECTED. The manifest recorded this report against hk_easy_2001, but the sample is a DIFFERENT recruited group: 700 patients enrolled in EASY between July 2001 and August 2003 (of whom 515 had schizophrenia or first-episode mania with psychotic features and 420 completed 3-year follow-up), not the 148 schizophrenia-spectrum entrants of 1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002 studied by chan2019/chan2020/chan2022. The two samples almost certainly share the 2001-2002 schizophrenia-spectrum entrants; neither report states the overlap, so it must not be pooled with any hk_easy_2001 result.
notes: The ONLY report in batch F01 with an employment count. Two subgroup results at 36 months (first-episode schizophrenia 111, first-episode psychotic mania 21). Both are BLOCKED (conflict_status = unresolved): the source contradicts itself about what sustained employment counts (Methods include full-time study, both table footnotes omit it) and, for the schizophrenia subgroup, about its denominator (111 with a printed 30.0% is impossible on the stated n = 374). 36 months falls in NO prespecified horizon band (t24m closes at 30, t60m opens at 48), so this report contributes to no landmark horizon even if the conflicts are resolved.

title: Prediction of functional remission in first-episode psychosis: 12-month follow-up of the randomized-controlled trial on extended early intervention in Hong Kong
cohort_overlap_notes: MANIFEST CORRECTED. The manifest recorded this report against hk_easy_2001. It is not that sample: it is a single-blinded randomised controlled trial (n = 160; extended EI 82, step-down care 78) recruited from patients who had ALREADY COMPLETED the 2-year EASY programme, so entry to this cohort required 2 years of prior EASY treatment. Recruitment dates are not stated in this report (methods are deferred to Chang et al. 2015), and the service is described as five clinical teams against the four teams described for 2001-2002 in chan2019/chan2020, so a shared recruitment era cannot be assumed. Separate cohort_id hk_easy_ext_rct, no overlaps_with row asserted because overlap cannot be established from this report.
notes: Employment appears ONLY as one necessary component of the composite functional remission outcome: FR required SOFAS > 60, RFS subscale thresholds AND being 'engaged in competitive employment (full-time or part-time work or studying)' at BOTH 6 and 12 months. Only the composite is counted (31/156, 19.9%); the employment component is never counted on its own. A composite of employment AND functioning-scale thresholds is not an employment construct and has no value in the outcome_construct vocabulary, so no outcome row is written. Note also that this source calls full-time study 'competitive employment', which the review's vocabulary does not.

journal: The Primary Care Companion For CNS Disorders
cohort_overlap_notes: COHORT CONFIRMED us_vha, same source cohort as lin2022. Figure 1 of this report and Figure 1 of lin2022 print the identical patient-selection cascade from the same database and the same study period: 132,153 with two or more schizophrenia diagnoses (1 Jan 2013 to 30 Sep 2019); 127,366 with one in the selection window (1 Jan 2014 to 30 Sep 2019); 125,595 enrolled in VA benefits for 12 months pre-index; 119,601 with a benefit record pre- and post-index; and an overall schizophrenia cohort of 119,343. notes: AUTHORSHIP: the article of record prints Benson C first and Lin D second, while Crossref, PubMed and the article's own 'To cite' line list Lin D first; report_id follows the article of record, as the manifest already decided. title: Long-Term Effects of Evidence-Based Supported Employment on Earnings and on SSI and SSDI Participation Among Individuals With Psychiatric Disabilities
cohort_overlap_notes: EIDP was a multisite trial at eight sites; detore2019 (cohort hartford_ips_rct) states in its acknowledgements that it 'was one of eight controlled trials of vocational rehabilitation programs, supported by cooperative #UD7 SM51818 ... as part of the Employment Intervention Demonstration Program (EIDP)', so the Hartford participants are EIDP participants and may fall inside the 1,648 enrolled here. Whether any of them are among the 449 in this long-term follow-up cannot be determined: this report says only that six of the eight sites joined the supplemental study and does not name them. Treat eidp_usa and hartford_ips_rct as possibly overlapping and do not pool them.
notes: Cohort confirmed as eidp_usa. Two nested samples: EIDP enrolled 1,648 at eight sites 1996-1998 and followed them 24 months; this report analyses the 449 from six sites who joined a supplemental economic study, consented to SSA data matching, were verified, and had a Disability Analysis File record. The 449 differ from the rest of EIDP on prior work, schizophrenia diagnosis, comorbidity, benefit status and region (Method, p. 1008-1009). The NSTW outcome (ever suspended or terminated from SSI/SSDI for work, 59/449) is a benefit-status outcome, not an employment construct, and is deliberately not extracted as a result. Figure 1 plots the yearly percentage with earned income but prints no counts, so no point-prevalence result is recoverable.

title: Disclosure of mental illness to prospective employers: Clinical, psychosocial, and work correlates in persons receiving supported employment
cohort_overlap_notes: The acknowledgements state this project 'was one of eight controlled trials of vocational rehabilitation programs, supported by cooperative #UD7 SM51818 ... as part of the Employment Intervention Demonstration Program (EIDP)', so hartford_ips_rct is an EIDP site and its participants overlap the EIDP cohort described by cook2016 (eidp_usa). Separately, the CT Dual Diagnosis Study (drake2015, ct_dual_diagnosis) recruited 1993-1998 from inner-city Hartford and Bridgeport community mental health centres with overlapping investigators; participant overlap with this Hartford sample is possible but nothing in either report evidences it.
notes: Cohort confirmed as hartford_ips_rct: a secondary analysis of the Hartford study of supported employment (Mueser et al. 2004), 204 participants randomised to IPS, a psychosocial clubhouse programme, or standard brokered vocational rehabilitation at Capitol Regional Mental Health Center, Hartford, Connecticut. The analysed sample of this paper is the 51 of the 68 IPS participants who obtained competitive work, i.e. selected on the outcome itself, so no employment proportion can be taken from it. The one extractable employment result is the 51 of 68 stated in Methods 2.1. Recruitment years, the diagnostic composition of the 204 and the outcomes of the clubhouse and standard vocational arms are not reported here.

title: Sex differences in outcomes of first episode psychosis: results from an early intervention service
cohort_overlap_notes: Ferrara is one of the Emilia-Romagna regional FEP programmes; the authors cite their own earlier Ferrara cohort papers (Belvederi Murri 2021, Ferrara 2019, 2024) which draw on the same service, so later reports of a Ferrara or Emilia-Romagna FEP cohort should be checked against eis_ferrara before pooling.
notes: Cohort confirmed as eis_ferrara. Five internal contradictions recorded in inconsistencies.md, three of which touch the employment results: the number screened (219 in Results 3.1 against 232 in Figure 1), the 24-month denominator (104 with 78 men in Results 3.2 against 101 with 76 men and 25 women in Figure 1 and Table 2, while Figure 1's own subtractions give 102 with 26 women), and the 12-month male NEET cell (printed 50 where the total and the printed 24.5% both require 25).

title: Longitudinal Course of Clients With Co-occurring Schizophrenia-Spectrum and Substance Use Disorders in Urban Mental Health Centers: A 7-Year Prospective Study
cohort_overlap_notes: Recruited 1993-1998 from two inner-city community mental health centres in Hartford and Bridgeport, Connecticut. detore2019's Hartford IPS trial (hartford_ips_rct) ran in the same city and era with overlapping investigators and the same state mental health authority; overlap is possible but neither report evidences it. The report also compares against a parallel New Hampshire Dual Diagnosis Study, which is a different cohort and contributes no result here.
notes: Cohort confirmed as ct_dual_diagnosis. report_quantifiable = no: the counts in Table 3 are printed, but no cell of the competitive-employment row is consistent with its own printed percentage on the column N (20/150 = 13% against 14%; 15/72 = 21% against 16%; 20/70 = 29% against 23%; 27/90 = 30% against 28%), so each cell has an unprinted denominator of its own and no numerator-denominator pair is recoverable without back-calculating. The triage figure of 27/90 at seven years is therefore not the proportion the paper reports. Advance Access 19 August 2015; the journal issue is 2016;42(1):202-211. report_id retains 2015.

title: Employment and income among first-time cases diagnosed with non-affective psychosis in Stockholm, Sweden: a follow-up study 2004/2005-2010
cohort_overlap_notes: Stockholm County Psychiatric Care System register cases 2005-2006 linked to LISA. Other Swedish register studies in the review (stockholm_2000, se_registers) may draw on overlapping populations and periods; check before pooling.
notes: Cohort confirmed as stockholm_2005. report_quantifiable = no. Employment is reported only as age-standardised NON-employment rates with confidence intervals, directly standardised to the Stockholm County 2005 population. A standardised rate is not a crude proportion, so neither its numerator nor its denominator exists to be read off, and its complement is not the employment proportion. No count of employed people appears anywhere in the report. The only counts printed for employment-adjacent variables are benefit receipt (study aid n = 147, sickness benefit n = 60, unemployment benefit n = 51 and so on), from which the number non-employed at baseline could only be obtained by dividing a count by a rounded percentage, which is barred.

title: Prospective Relationships Between Motivation and Functioning in Recovery After a First Episode of Schizophrenia
cohort_overlap_notes: RAISE-ETP is a multi-report cohort. Any other RAISE-ETP or NAVIGATE report in the review shares these 404 participants and must share cohort_id raise_etp; OnTrackNY (ontracky_ny) is a different programme and a different cohort.
notes: Cohort confirmed as raise_etp. report_quantifiable = no. Table 1 prints only percentages for the SURF work-or-school variable with no numerator, and its footnote gives a single range across all variables ('Ns range from 257 (12 mo) to 404 (baseline)') rather than a denominator per variable per timepoint. The measure is also a composite of paid work OR being a student, combined from three SURF items and then aggregated across 6-month blocks, so the printed percentage is the mean of an aggregated score and need not be a person-level proportion at all: 39.8% is not n/404 for any integer n. RAISE-ETP is cluster randomised by site (34 sites); this report pools both allocation groups and enters treatment group as a moderator.

cohort_overlap_notes: Jockey Club Early Psychosis (JCEP) project, Hong Kong, recruited June 2009 to August 2011, aged 26-55. notes: The 4-year employment cell prints ONLY 'Unemployed, n (%) 40 (65.6%) / 21 (34.4%)'. Those percentages are ROW percentages of the 61 unemployed (40/61 = 65.6%, 21/61 = 34.4%), not column percentages of the group sizes 112 and 107, so the table supplies no evidence at all about the denominator on which the employment variable was observed. title: Effectiveness of an Assertive Community Treatment program for people with severe schizophrenia in mainland China - a 12-month randomized controlled trial
notes: NEAR-ZERO CELL CONFIRMED as printed: 10/30 ACT v 1/28 control. Recorded exactly as printed with no continuity correction. TWO CORRECTIONS to the triage note: (a) the ascertainment is any_time_during_followup, not point prevalence, because the counts are of patients who 'returned to wage-earning employment ... over the 12-month follow-up'; (b) 'selected for severe impairment' is not an employment-related criterion under D9, so employment selection is coded unclear on incomplete reporting, not selected. Allocated arms only: no whole-cohort row, because the ACT team included a part-time employment specialist and worked on 'setting goals for employment', so employment_targeted_intervention would be yes.

title: Symptomatic, functional and service utilization outcomes of migrants with a first episode of psychosis
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED IN PART. 594/1196 is confirmed as a SUM of the two printed subgroup counts (migrants 137/293 and Australian-born 457/903; Table 3, p. 1394), not a printed total. COMPOSITE work-or-study CONFIRMED: paid_or_education, not paid_any, and the source gives no paid-only numerator. DISCHARGE TIMING CONFIRMED as a followup_basis problem: occupation is measured at discharge from EPPIC, elapsed follow-up varies (median duration of care 581 days for migrants against 667 for Australian-born, IQR 333-730 and 478-741), so followup_basis = calendar_end_common and the result is barred from every landmark horizon. NEW FINDING: the migrant figure is printed twice and differently, 46.8 per cent in Table 3 against 47.3 per cent in the text on p. 1395, so the migrant row and the derived whole-cohort row are blocked with conflict_status = unresolved.

title: Employment trajectories until midlife in schizophrenia and other psychoses: the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966
cohort_overlap_notes: shares cohort with: majuri2021, rautio2016 | MULTIPLE INCLUDED REPORTS, apply result selection rule. Result selection was applied across all three and resolved to NO CHANGE: see report_cohort_map.csv and unresolved_queries.md.
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED. Latent-class employment trajectories only. Table 2 (p. 70) gives membership counts in five trajectory classes (traditional, highly educated, self-employed, delayed full-time, floundering) over ages 16 to 45. A trajectory class is a 30-year longitudinal pattern, not a prevalence at a timepoint, and is not recorded as one. NO OUTCOME ROW IS CREATED. The one other candidate, Table 1's Statistics Finland socioeconomic status at age 46, is deliberately NOT summed into a paid_any count: (a) it is a register socioeconomic classification the report never presents as employment status; (b) its residual category is printed as 'others, mostly unemployed', so zero work is NOT separable from every category containing positive paid work and D12.3 bars the derivation, exactly as for rautio2016's '<25 per cent' band; (c) it is measured at chronological age 46, which D12.3b bars from every horizon; and (d) the SZ-men column's own cells sum to 28 against a printed column header of 29. report_quantifiable = no.

title: Schizophrenia and work: aspects related to job acquisition in a follow-up study
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED ON BOTH POINTS. CRITICAL SELECTION confirmed and quoted: the sample is 'individuals ... who expressed a desire for employment' and 'a convenience sample ... of schizophrenics desiring employment', all of whom then completed a prevocational training group, so employment_selection_status = selected. The 35.8 per cent inconsistency is confirmed and is worse than the triage note says: 19/45 = 42.2 per cent, 35.8 per cent requires a base of 53, and the job-duration bands on p. 38 (6.8, 13.6 and 22.7 per cent for 3, 6 and 10 people) imply a THIRD base of 44. conflict_status = unresolved; no denominator was reconstructed.

title: Cognitive remediation for vocational rehabilitation nonresponders
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED, WORDING REFINED. Selection is established by inclusion criteria b and c: 'currently enrolled in a vocational rehabilitation program for at least 3 months' and 'has not benefited from recent vocational rehabilitation, defined as either has not worked for the past 3 months ... or having a recent unsuccessful ending of a job'. The triage phrase 'seeking work' is NOT in the paper and is not used; the recorded reason is prior_employment_failure, with vocational-service enrolment and a baseline no-work requirement also present. NEW FINDINGS: (a) all three whole-sample employment outcomes are any_time_during_followup over 36 months, never point prevalence; (b) Table 3's E-VR cells print '12/26' beside '48%', and 12/26 is 46.2 per cent, while 12/25 is exactly 48 per cent and Table 1's work-history rows for E-VR sum to 25; (c) the Discussion's whole-sample figures of 54 per cent competitive and 67 per cent any work activity contradict the table counts, which give 28/54 = 51.9 and 34/54 = 63.0 per cent. Four of the six result rows are therefore blocked as unresolved.

title: Effects of the Indianapolis Vocational Intervention Program (IVIP) on defeatist beliefs, work motivation, and work outcomes in serious mental illness
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED ON SELECTION, REFUTED ON CONSTRUCT. Selection confirmed and quoted: participants were 'deemed not ready for supported employment by their referring clinician', with 'no placement or no history of success in past 6 months the requisite'. CONSTRUCT: the outcome is NOT recorded as paid_any and NOT as paid_competitive. The report never states that the supported employment counted was paid, never names an employer, wage or labour-market setting, and uses 'enrolled in supported employment' (Methods 2.5.1.3 and 2.6) interchangeably with 'secure supported employment' (Results, p. 132) and 'supported employment enrollment status'. Under SAP 3.1 an activity whose remuneration cannot be established is not paid work, and the codebook routes an unestablished labour-market setting to outcome_construct = unclear. The $10 per hour that IS stated applies to the four-month work therapy placement that BOTH arms received, not to the outcome. See unresolved_queries.md. SEPARATE ISSUE: recruitment is described as from 'community mental health clinics affiliated with the New York State Psychiatric Institute' with NYSPI ethics approval, which does not match the cohort slug institute_living_rct or the Hartford author affiliations.

title: The association between relapse and the outcome of schizophrenia and recurrent psychotic disorders
notes: TRIAGE CONFIRMED. Composite EET confirmed: 'employment status, categorised as being or not being in employment, education or training' names all three, so paid_or_education_or_training. Both arms pooled confirmed: 'The present analysis treats participants recruited to the trial as a single cohort' and 'For all analyses, we combined data from both randomised groups'. Established psychosis confirmed; the whole-cohort mean age is not printed but the sample-size-weighted mean of the two printed subgroup means is 46.3 years. NEW FINDING, and the one that matters: the 190 participants with EET status are split IRRECONCILABLY. Table 2 (p. 676) gives 8/66 and 30/124; the Results text (p. 674) gives completion of 70.7 per cent of 82 relapsers and 77.2 per cent of 171 non-relapsers, i.e. 58 and 132; and Table 4 (p. 676) totals 57, 132 and 189. The same text percentages reproduce the MANSA and PANSS denominators exactly, so they are not loose rounding. Every EET row is blocked with conflict_status = unresolved.

title: Factors Associated With Real-Life Functioning in Persons With Schizophrenia in a 4-Year Follow-up Study of the Italian Network for Research on Psychoses

Neither is in the screened set; no other NIRP report is in this review.

title: Vocational Rehabilitation in Young Adults With Incident Schizophrenia - A Danish Retrospective Cohort Study
cohort_overlap_notes: OPUS here is the routine Danish OPUS early-intervention SERVICE at Aarhus and Aalborg with OPUS start dates 1 Jan 2014 to 31 Dec 2019. It is NOT the 1998-2000 OPUS randomised trial (opus_1998; hansen2024, hansen2024b). The recruitment windows do not overlap and OPUS admits only incident first-episode patients, so no individual can be in both. Participants are inside Danish national register cohorts (dk_registers_1998, dk_registers_birth) and inside the qualitative sub-study Ortenblad et al. 2025.
notes: Two non-randomised groups (Morpheus n=116 at Aarhus, standard vocational rehabilitation n=130 at Aalborg), both restricted at entry to patients neither employed nor in education but motivated to be. No whole recruited cohort exists for a prevalence estimate: 246 is the union of two site-defined selected groups and the report never prints a combined count.

Follow-up is engagement in a programme running March 2006 to February 2013; no per-participant elapsed follow-up is ever reported.

title: Psychotic Disorders in Adolescence and Later Long-term Exclusion From Education and Employment
cohort_overlap_notes: 1987 Finnish Birth Cohort, whole-population register linkage. Participants are inside Finnish nationwide register cohorts (fi_registers; hakulinen2019, hakulinen2020, batch F08) and inside other 1987 Finnish Birth Cohort reports. These must not be treated as independent samples.
